title: Rota retrospective + incident summaries (week of 2026-08-12)
content:
Purpose: quick rota retrospective + concise incident summaries to share with product & infra partners. Mostly shorthand; expand if you want a formal postmortem.

Context and high-level takeaways:
- This week we had two customer-impacting incidents (INC-3241, INC-3257) plus multiple small flaps that added noise to oncall.
- Root causes were unrelated: one was a runtime cache eviction ordering bug exposed by a quantization change; the other was a control-plane regression in the rollout manager.
- SLO pressure: streaming-gen P99 latency crept above objective for a 45m window during INC-3241. Error budget for streaming gen is now ~72% remaining for the quarter.
- Operational improvements recommended: stricter canary gating for kernel/quantization changes, add a rollout throttle to rollout-manager, and an immediate runbook tweak for streaming latency investigation steps.

Incidents (short form)
1) INC-3241 — streaming P99 spike (2026-08-14 02:10–02:55 UTC)
- Impact: 3rd-party customers using streaming API saw P99 latency increase from ~220ms to ~1.2s; some streaming connections reset. Estimated affected requests: ~18k.
- Detection: alerted via latency-SLO breach rule -> SEV2 escalation.
- Timeline (brief):
  * 02:10 - latency alert fires (oncall paging Victor)
  * 02:15 - oncall triage identifies correlation with recent runtime canary (quantization kernel swap) deployed 01:58
  * 02:25 - rollback of canary triggered (automated rollback patched during incident)
  * 02:35 - partial recovery observed; P99 trending down
  * 02:55 - metrics back within SLO; incident declared mitigated
- Root cause (initial): cache eviction ordering + kernel variant interacting poorly with KV cache metadata; when sequence lengths > 1024 and certain attention kernel enabled, KV cache index rebuild triggered extra work per token and blocked async batching.
- Mitigation performed: rolled back canary -> immediate improvement; applied a temporary config flag to force eager KV cache operations to a safer path for affected hosts.
- Follow-ups / owners (action items):
  * ENG-serving-runtime: add unit/integration test for kv-cache + kernel variant combos (owner: Sara Liu, due 2026-09-03)
  * Release-engineering: add a pre-rollout check for quantization/kernel combos that are on the compatibility matrix (owner: Amir Patel, due 2026-08-26)
  * Product/Console: add a health widget for streaming P95/P99 grouped by kernel variant to make regressions visible during canaries (owner: Lina Gomez, due 2026-09-10)

2) INC-3257 — rollout-manager stuck in retry loop (2026-08-16 11:40–13:05 UTC)
- Impact: Canary rollouts for Dedicated customers stalled; autoscale decisions delayed causing transient throughput drops for two Dedicated clusters. No customer-facing API errors but reduced throughput for ~90 minutes. Classified SEV3.
- Detection: internal rollout-manager error-storm log alert + pager to infra-oncall.
- Timeline (brief):
  * 11:40 - rollout-manager enters retry loop after malformed update from control-plane
  * 11:50 - infra-oncall disables auto-rollout for pending batches to stop churn
  * 12:20 - fix deployed that validates control-plane payloads and rejects malformed ones; rollout resumed at 12:40
  * 13:05 - stability confirmed; incident mitigated
- Root cause: regression in a schema validation change that allowed empty-change deltas to be processed, which caused an infinite retry path in rollout-manager under particular timing.
- Follow-ups / owners:
  * Platform-engineering: revert + add stronger schema validation + add unit tests (owner: Omar Haddad, due 2026-08-24)
  * Observability: add a rollout-manager metric for retry-count with alert threshold (owner: Pablo Ruiz, due 2026-08-28)

Other noisy items / small flaps
- 2026-08-13 07:00 UTC: ephemeral post-deploy DNS TTL mismatch on one region; auto-healed via traffic-engineering. Note: update DNS deploy checklist (owner: Ethan Morales).
- Two minor SEV4s for ingress rate-limiting config drift on dev clusters — root cause was inconsistent config sync from infra-config-service; short-term fix applied.

SLO snapshot (weekly)
- Streaming generation latency (P99): objective = 350ms; last week median = 210ms; breach window for INC-3241 accounts for a single 45m uplift; weekly P99 aggregated = 290ms.
- API availability: objective = 99.95%; current week = 99.97% after accounting for rollback.
- Error budget (quarterly) for streaming-gen: started at 100% on July 1; now ~72% remaining (approx). See linked spreadsheet if you want per-customer burn rates.

Oncall handoff notes (for next rotation)
- Current oncall: Victor (primary), Maya (secondary). Next rotation: Victor -> Naomi on 2026-08-20 07:00 UTC.
- Hand-off checklist (quick):
  * Confirm active incidents: none open (all mitigated); make sure follow-ups assigned in Jira
  * Confirm overrides: rollback lock for runtime canaries enabled until follow-ups completed (ticket JIRA-3250)
  * Check for planned releases: runtime 1.14.2 scheduled 2026-08-21 — postpone canary until kv-cache test added (Sara's action)
  * Costly customer jobs: Dedicated-cust-44 has scheduled heavy eval run 2026-08-20 14:00 UTC; advise capacity owner to pin to dedicated pool and not to shared hosts
  * Known flaky alerts to mute: test-cluster connectivity flaps (alert: test-cluster-ping-failure); mute until 2026-08-21 to reduce noise during handoff (owner: SRE rotation)

Rota retrospective notes (ops process/culture)
- What went well:
  * Fast detection via SLO-based paging (latency-rule proved useful)
  * Clear owner consensus during incident -> rollback performed quickly
  * Automated rollback mechanism worked as intended for canary
- What could be better:
  * Canary gating around kernel/quantization combos was too permissive; need compatibility matrix enforcement before rollout to reduce blast radius.
  * Oncall cognitive load: multiple small alerts + one major incident made triage harder. Recommendation: improve alert grouping and signal-to-noise (observability team item).
  * Post-incident comms: need a lighter template for ad-hoc status updates for customers (short status + ETA) so SRE doesn't become comms bottleneck.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Do we want a hard block in CI that prevents kernel variants from being rolled into canary if the kv-cache test has not passed? (ops vs runtime tradeoffs)
- Should rollout-manager have an automated circuit-breaker that pauses rollouts when retry-count crosses N per minute? (proposal: N=5; owner: platform-engineering to draft)

Quick TODOs (who -> what -> due)
- Sara Liu -> add kv-cache + kernel-variant integration test -> 2026-09-03
- Omar Haddad -> revert rollout-manager schema change + unit tests -> 2026-08-24
- Lina Gomez -> streaming health widget in Console -> 2026-09-10
- Pablo Ruiz -> rollout retry-count metric + alert -> 2026-08-28
- Victor (oncall) -> ensure JIRA follow-ups created and linked to this doc -> 2026-08-20

Notes to self (Priya):
- Draft a short external-facing status template and circulate to product comms.
- Pair with runtime team next Wed to walk through kv-cache internals (booked Fri 2026-08-21 16:00 UTC).

Appendix (links and quick refs):
- Incident board: https://redwood-ops.example/incident/INC-3241
- Postmortem skeleton (to use if needed): https://confluence.redwood.example/display/SRE/Postmortem+Template
- SLO dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.example/dashboards/slo-streaming-gen

End of notes.
